{"id":"mimid-1wgh.114.7","title":"mimid terminating calls: an SFU of its own, so IRC and stream edges have something to call","description":"Mark 2026-11-23: "i wonder if there is a way for mimid to also terminate
calls and put them in a call group" and "the idea is to give irc and
binary edgepoints something to call too".

THE MOTIVATION, which decides the shape. mimid's non-JMAP front ends have
no media stack. IRC already carries the LINK kind of call (bead
mimid-1wgh.114.3: paste a conference URL, the channel sees it, click it
in a browser), and today that URL points at somebody else's service. If
mimid terminated calls, the link would point at the user's OWN provider.

WHAT AN SFU BUYS, and the guides already settle the mechanics.
jmap-vtc-e2ee-guide.md §2: with WebRTC Encoded Transform or SFrame "the
SFU sees encrypted frames and forwards them by SSRC -- it cannot decode,
mix, or transcode". So terminating the TRANSPORT does not mean seeing the
MEDIA. The guide also names which SFUs forward opaque payloads
(mediasoup, Jitsi Videobridge, Pion, LiveKit) and which break E2EE by
decoding (Janus's VideoRoom plugin by default, Opal entirely, being an
MCU), and warns that simulcast or thumbnailing that inspects frames
breaks it too. Choosing the SFU is therefore a correctness decision, not
a preference.

It also answers the TURN problem properly. Decision: the default relays
are ParlorVTC's public ones (commit c46f9dba), which is the arrangement
draft-atwood-jmap-vtc-00 §NAT Traversal Is Not Negotiated warns about --
both ends relaying through one third party, which learns both addresses
and that those two spoke. A provider-run SFU replaces that with a relay
the participant's own provider runs, which already knows their address
because they connect to it.

THE HARD LIMIT, and it is the trap in this idea: A LINK-JOINED
PARTICIPANT IS NOT AN MLS MEMBER, so their media cannot be keyed by the
call room's group. media_secret is derived from an epoch of a group, and
a browser that followed a link is not in it. "mimid terminates calls so
IRC can call too" sounds like it gives IRC the keyed call. It cannot.

SO THERE IS A FORK, and it is Mark's:
(a) The SFU holds a key for link-joined participants, mixes or relays for
    them, and the call is NOT end-to-end encrypted against the provider.
    Honest, useful, and must be labelled: AGENTS.md forbids describing
    mimid as protecting against a malicious provider, and a client MUST
    NOT show such a call as end-to-end encrypted.
(b) A link-joined call is a SEPARATE call from the MLS-keyed one, with
    its own secret (minted, fragment-only), encrypted among
    link-holders and authenticating nobody. That is ParlorVTC's model.
    Two kinds of call, named differently to the user.
(c) The SFU forwards only, and a link-joined participant gets nothing:
    the link is for people whose client can be an MLS member. Keeps one
    kind of call and leaves IRC where it is.

WHAT IT COSTS. An SFU is a large component of a kind mimid does not
contain: real-time media, not request and response. A call page for a
clicked link is a UI, which decision mimid-1wgh.38 says mimid does not
ship -- so either that decision gets an exception or the page lives
elsewhere (ParlorVTC is two HTML files and ~1100 lines with no build
step, which is the shape to copy). And the provider learns who is in
which call for how long, which it largely does already.

NOT A BLOCKER FOR ANYTHING BUILT. Signalling, the keying, the call room
and the JMAP surface all work without it.

new_value: {"notes":"THE FORK IS DECIDED: mimid-1wgh.123, option (b). A link-joined call is a separate call with its own minted secret, encrypted among link-holders and authenticating nobody, named differently to the user. Option (a), the SFU holding a key for them, was rejected because it makes one call whose security property differs per participant, which no interface can explain honestly."}

{"notes":"THE FORK IS DECIDED: mimid-1wgh.123, option (b). A link-joined call is a separate call with its own minted secret, encrypted among link-holders and authenticating nobody, named differently to the user. Option (a), the SFU holding a key for them, was rejected because it makes one call whose security property differs per participant, which no interface can explain honestly.
ARCHITECTURE, Mark asked 2026-11-23 whether the SFU is part of the mimid
binary or a separate one that can run elsewhere. SEPARATE, and the
strongest reason is the correction on decision mimid-1wgh.123: a
forwarding-only SFU needs no keys for either kind of call, so it is
plumbing rather than a party to the call, and can run anywhere under
anyone.

THE OTHER REASONS, each sufficient on its own:
- It is a different kind of program. mimid is request and response over
  a journal and SQLite; an SFU is soft-real-time packet forwarding at
  thousands of packets a second per participant. In one process a slow
  SQLite write adds jitter to someone's audio.
- It scales on a different axis: hubs with rooms, SFUs with concurrent
  call-minutes. And an SFU wants to sit near the PARTICIPANTS for
  round-trip time while a hub wants to sit where its data is.
- Its exposure is far worse: attacker-controlled RTP over UDP from
  anywhere is a nastier parsing surface than JMAP over TLS, and it
  should not share a process with the MLS state and the hub's signing
  key. #![forbid(unsafe_code)] helps; a process boundary helps more.
- crate-jmap already assumes it: crate-jmap-vtc-livekit, -aws and
  -ffmpeg are adapters to an external media plane. The realistic SFUs
  (mediasoup, Pion, LiveKit, Jitsi Videobridge) are separate processes
  in other languages whatever we do.

WHAT BELONGS IN MIMID: the control-plane glue only -- tell the SFU a
call exists and who may join, tell a client where to connect. That is
ordinary request and response and fits the existing crates. The media
plane is the separate thing, and mimid may not need to write it at all."}
